locus: §4.6a, "What this section reports is best read as a proposal for a **measure**"
current:
What this section reports is best read as a proposal for a **measure**:
socioeconomic position scored not by a categorical class schema but by the
occupational content the schema summarises. Each legislator's prior
occupation, coded to O\*NET, is scored on an organisational-**altitude**
ladder — bottom, middle, top of a hierarchy — plus a level the categorical
schemas do not carry: **free work**, occupations that sit outside the
organisational hierarchy altogether. The move has ancestry: Weeden and
Grusky's case for measuring class at the disaggregated occupation level,
and Kohn and Schooler's occupational self-direction, where closeness of
supervision explained class differences in psychology, are the two nearest
lines. What this measure adds is the off-ladder level — position scored not
only as altitude within the hierarchy but as distance from it — and that
axis is not a post-hoc reading: the ordering **free < front-line <
corporate** was preregistered before any occupational element was joined
to the register, and found. What follows are the measure's
results — the U over its levels, the off-ladder level's stability across
three decades, and, in the joint model below, the absorption of the class
label the measure refines.
proposed:
This section proposes a **measure**: socioeconomic position scored not by a
categorical class schema but by the occupational content the schema
summarises. Each legislator's prior occupation, coded to O\*NET, is scored on
an organisational-**altitude** ladder — bottom, middle, top of a hierarchy —
plus a level the categorical schemas do not carry: **free work**, occupations
that sit outside the organisational hierarchy altogether. Two lines of prior
work run nearest: Weeden and Grusky argued for measuring class at the
disaggregated occupation level, and Kohn and Schooler located the
class–psychology link in occupational self-direction, closeness of
supervision above all. What this measure adds is the off-ladder level —
position scored not only as altitude within the hierarchy but as distance
from it — and that axis is not a post-hoc reading: the ordering **free <
front-line < corporate** was preregistered before any occupational element
was joined to the register, and found. What follows are the measure's
results — the U over its levels, the off-ladder level's stability across
three decades, and, in the joint model below, the absorption of the class
label the measure refines.
rationale: The ancestry sentence strands its verb ("are") thirty words after its compound subject and then spends the stress position on the flat "the two nearest lines"; recasting Weeden/Grusky and Kohn/Schooler as agents of real verbs puts each claim's substance at the close. The opening likewise gains from an agent-plus-verb subject rather than "What this section reports is best read as."
